who: Lindy Biggs, historian of technology and industry at Auburn University.

evidence.says: The authority for Lindy Biggs cites The Rational Factory (1996) and identifies its author with Auburn University’s Department of History.
Michael James Zarafonitis’s 2010 Auburn dissertation, The Fabulous Fox Theatre and Atlanta, names Lindy Biggs, associate professor of history, as committee chair.

notes: The authority’s affiliation and a listed student’s dissertation directly establish the match.

who: Marvin B. Becker, historian of medieval and Renaissance Italy at Rochester and Michigan; PhD Pennsylvania 1950.

evidence.says: The Marvin B. Becker authority cites Florence in Transition and Medieval Italy.
The AHA memorial attributes both books to Marvin B. Becker, records his Pennsylvania doctorate in 1950 and Rochester appointment, and names James Banker among his doctoral students.
The Rochester bulletin lists Marvin B. Becker as professor of history with a Pennsylvania PhD.

notes: Matching books, doctorate, university, and listed doctoral student distinguish n81012468 from the other candidates.

who: Brett A. Berliner, historian of modern Europe and France at Morgan State; history PhD Massachusetts Amherst.

evidence.says: The Brett A. Berliner authority identifies him as author of Ambivalent Desire (2002).
Morgan State identifies Brett Berliner as an associate professor, gives his history PhD from Massachusetts Amherst, and lists Ambivalent Desire among his publications.
The university’s 2017 faculty research profiles also list Berliner in History and Geography with the same doctorate and book.

notes: The shared book connects the LC identity to the faculty member at the students’ university during their period.

who: Joseph R. Berrigan, historian of the Italian Renaissance at Georgia, 1966–1997; PhD Tulane.

evidence.says: The Joseph R. Berrigan authority cites The Patriarch and the Prince (1982).
The catalogue identifies the editors of The Patriarch and the Prince as Despina Stratoudaki White and Joseph R. Berrigan, Jr.
The Athens Banner-Herald obituary identifies Joseph R. Berrigan as a Tulane history PhD specializing in the Italian Renaissance, teaching at Georgia from 1966 until 1997.

notes: The university, period, doctorate, and publication with listed student Despina White support n82008390. The Joseph E. candidate is a legal author.

who: The record appears to refer to Thomas Robert (Robert) Travers, historian of British imperial India at Cornell.

evidence.says: NEH identifies Thomas Robert Travers at Cornell in 2014, researching Indian petitioning and British imperial history; associated publications use Robert Travers.
Christina Casey’s 2017 Cornell dissertation thanks Dr. Travers for bringing her to Cornell to work with him and for sustained guidance; its committee also included Weil and Ghosh.
Thomas A’Beckett Travers is identified as an ophthalmologist whose cited work concerns strabismus treatment.
Thomas Travers, author of Peripheralizing DeLillo, is identified as an independent scholar with an English-literature doctorate from Birkbeck.
Thomas J. D. Travers is identified only through Baron Baby’s Evil Plan for World Domination and the Annihilation of Adults (2006), without a university or doctorate.

notes: The ophthalmologist and literature scholar do not match. No evidence establishes the fiction author’s identity or links him to Cornell; that candidate remains unresolved.

who: Ivan T. Berend, historian of European economic and social history at UCLA from 1990; retired 2015.

evidence.says: UCLA identifies Ivan T. Berend as a history professor who joined in 1990 and specializes in nineteenth- and twentieth-century European social and economic history.
UCLA’s 2015 retirement account records twenty-five years on its faculty and names graduate student Grace Ballor among the speakers.
This authority identifies an economist named Iván Berend through Fejlesztésiberuházási politika (1975), rather than the UCLA historian’s works.
The item bearing LC n84079030 identifies the separate economist Iván Berend and links his economics authority records.

notes: The supplied LC record belongs to the development-policy economist Iván Berend, a different author from UCLA historian Iván T. Berend.

who: Imre Josef Demhardt, historian of cartography at UT Arlington since 2008; geography PhD Frankfurt 1995.

evidence.says: The Imre Josef Demhardt authority cites Deutsche Kolonialgrenzen in Afrika and Die Entschleierung Afrikas.
The publisher identifies author Imre Josef Demhardt as a historian and geographer holding the history-of-cartography chair at UT Arlington since 2008.
The 2019 nomination CV identifies Imre Josef Demhardt as professor in Arlington’s History Department, with a Frankfurt geography PhD in 1995 and Darmstadt habilitation in 2001.

notes: The full name, field, and university support the match. The AHA Darmstadt entry corresponds to his habilitation, not his PhD.

who: C. Elizabeth Raymond, American cultural and western historian at the University of Nevada, Reno.

evidence.says: The authority identifies C. Elizabeth Raymond, expanded as Catherine Elizabeth Raymond, through George Wingfield and a Nevada Historical Society publication.
The university library identifies Elizabeth Raymond as a Reno history professor and author of George Wingfield: Owner and Operator of Nevada.
A 2017 university news listing identifies Elizabeth Raymond as a history professor at the University of Nevada, Reno.

notes: The exact name and shared George Wingfield book identify the LC candidate; the university affiliation is documented in the students’ period.
